items.summary: Disposition: evidence_needed. Risk is high for public exposure and security-sensitive releases, and medium for bounded reversible growth. Concrete evidence: fleet-doctor has no run or control results; operations deploy-health, uptime, and error sweeps have no results; all 59 security sitefacts are unknown. Authentication and access boundaries, secrets exposure, container isolation, release/deploy controls, dependency provenance, complete TLS posture, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unverified. No incident or exploitation is evidenced, and no certificates are reported expiring within 30 days; neither establishes a clean bill of health. Exact decision: keep public exposure and security-sensitive releases blocked; continue only ordinary reversible work that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, new data collection, or cross-site behavior. Continue the existing read-only security evidence matrix using dated, redacted evidence; do not access credentials or private containers, alter permissions or configuration, deploy, exploit targets, or conduct outreach.

The retained task-routing change is conditionally acceptable from a security perspective because it changes ownership metadata only and does not modify code, credentials, permissions, dependencies, telemetry, deployment, or production behavior. Require focused routing validation, uniqueness/deduplication evidence, attribution, and reversible rollback before completion.
